$comment: template_version: 0.1.0. Schema v0 (#16): only the columns needed to write scenario A (Keycloak). Columns found missing or unneeded are listed in research/template-design/v0-columns.md and handed to #3. Which columns must be filled for which decision is rule R1 of claim_lint (tools/claim_lint/RULES.md), not this schema, so that a missing column is reported with a rule ID.
title: Claim registry v0

scenario.description: Scenario of the casestudy this registry is written for (A, B, C) or a free name

casestudy_commit.description: Commit of jwt-claims-casestudy that catalog_ref points into

name.description: Claim name as it appears in the JSON object (without the namespace)

namespace.description: Name of the namespace object the claim sits in (e.g. https://claims.example.com/), or null for a top-level claim

catalog_refs.description: Rows of the casestudy claim list (name and type are owned there). A list, because the list has one row per defining source (RFC 9068 for the access token, OIDC Core for the ID token ...)

volatility.description: Seconds allowed between a change of the value and its reflection in the token. 0 means the value never changes for the subject

propagation_delay.description: Worst-case seconds until a change reaches the consumers (bounded by the token lifetime when only exp ends it)

carried_in.description: IDs of token types (token_types.yaml) that carry the claim

max_bytes.description: Worst-case UTF-8 bytes of one value as serialized in JSON, without the quotes of a string (after JSON escaping)

max_items.description: Worst-case number of elements when shape is array

enum: 問い合わせに切り替える
上限で固定（超えない値域）

integrity_until.description: Places where the value is copied out of the signed token, so that the JWS no longer protects it (header, DB session context, queue, logs). Early form of the integrity_until column of #3; free text in v0
